correction_2026_09_29: Values unchanged; verdict_source, the verdicts and the conclusion are corrected here. (1) verdict_source: only nemotron_verdict was run under the calibration/CoT prompt (nemotron_judge_test.py:78-124). llama_verdict and qwen_verdict are Project v1's stored verdicts (nemotron_judge_test.py:13). Project v1's repository (github.com/deepset01-sys/medisimplifier-nebius, not part of this repo) at commit dd6681b shows that run used a one-word prompt, one user message and max_tokens 2000 (perturbation_calibration.py:193-227), and its results/nebius_evidence/calibration_verdicts.json equals these two columns on 708/708 rows. In this file Llama's column repeats one verdict per item index (results/tau_recompute_v1_matched.json idx_repeat_check). The three judges did not share a prompt. (2) The sign change from the reference to the cells comes from the drop share, not the labels. The reference has 138 drops in 333 items (0.414), the cells 9 to 20 (0.027 to 0.093), and Phi_V depends on that share. In B/strict, adding Nemotron raises the controls' mean b^2 and lowers the drops'; below 0.128 the rise outweighs the fall (pairings.published_mixed_prompt.cells['B/strict'].mechanism.mean_b2_breakeven), and the Delta Phi_V point estimate is negative up to 0.16 (delta_sign_runs_on_grid). Reweighted to 0.414, every cell is positive with a CI above 0 (B/strict +0.0718 [+0.0046, +0.1154]); the reference reweighted to B/strict's 0.027 is -0.1931 [-0.2541, -0.1343]. The bands were applied across different drop shares, so 'REFUTED', 'reverses sign' and 'label-contamination artifact' do not follow, and 'never positive' holds only at the cells' own 0.027 to 0.093 shares. (3) With all three judges under the deployed prompt (results/gate_calibration_full.json), the reference cell is +0.0438 at its own 0.429 share, as in results/consensus_accuracy.json (+0.0426 [+0.0264, +0.0593] at 0.414); the four cells are -0.0697 to -0.0287 at their own shares, each inside or below the 95% range of a shuffled Nemotron column with the same flag rate, and +0.0323 to +0.0502 at 0.414, where the CIs of A/strict, B/strict and B/generous include 0 and A/generous's (+0.0502 [+0.0041, +0.0944]) does not. What stands: split_f_diagnostic and the 128/150 PRESENT count, so the automated labels were wrong; 9 genuine drops cannot show the sign of Nemotron's effect. scripts/run_tau_recompute_v1.py reproduces every value in this file (asserted) and writes results/tau_recompute_v1_matched.json; docs/judgebench_v2_protocol_erratum.md has the full comparison.
conclusion: All four clean-tau cells REFUTED. Primary (B/strict) delta_phi_v = -0.144 [-0.195,-0.098]; every cell negative; most generous (A/generous) -0.029, CI straddles 0, never positive. The published +0.071 reverses sign under hand-verified labels: it was a label-contamination artifact — Nemotron's over-flagging (65% FP on perturbed-but-faithful items vs 34% on pristine controls) was credited as recall against the ~85%-mislabeled positive class. Caveat: positive class small (9-20), CIs wide, tau still synthetic; a real diagnosis-drop claim requires physician-anchored tau.
